judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A license granted in perpetuity' is short and definite, though the section heading promises 'TERM AND OPTIONS' and no options appear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A perpetual, non-terminable licence is hard to reconcile with Section 16, which assumes 'the termination of this Agreement', and with 3(b)'s reference to 'during the Term ... or thereafter'; there is no termination mechanism anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Royalty free and fully paid' is clear; 'solely entitled to all economic benefits' is broad but unidirectional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 6(d)'s equal division of infringement recoveries within Morton's Territories, a modest tension with 'solely entitled to all economic benefits'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All or substantially all of his assets and/or rights', 'initiate negotiations and ... negotiate in good faith' and the interplay of the 30-day and six-month periods leave the trigger and duration of the right of first offer genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 10's unrestricted right to sublicense or franchise 'any or all' rights and Section 18's binding effect on transferees and assigns, which together could let Licensee achieve a transfer without ever triggering this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is unqualified — 'any or all of the rights' — with a flow-down requirement stated in general terms and no consent condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unrestricted sublicence/franchise right can be used to circumvent 9(c)'s first-offer right and sits uneasily with 3(a)'s reservation and 4's quality controls, which reach Licensee's own operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is asymmetric — irreparable harm is conceded for any Licensee breach but for Licensor only as to the Nevada covenant — and 'as applicable and appropriate' is loose, but the drafting is deliberate rather than obscure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Promising court injunctions overlaps 5(b)'s grant of injunctive power to arbitrators and 5(a)'s mandatory arbitration of quality disputes, so which forum enjoins a quality breach is unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver clause in familiar language with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 22, which requires waivers to be in a signed writing; the two are complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery/deemed-receipt rules are mechanical, though telecopy notice depends on the recipient 'acknowledg[ing]' receipt, which is self-defeating in a dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Licensor's notice address is given as 'Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.' although Section 1(n) defines Licensor as Rank Licensing, Inc., a mismatch with the defined party.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not use the name or credit of Licensor in any manner whatsoever' is startlingly broad given the licence itself, and 'coupled with an interest' is a legal term of art used loosely here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The absolute bar on using Licensor's name is in tension with the licence granted in 2(a) and with 8(a)'s cross-promotion duties, and the 'no power ... coupled with an interest' language sits oddly with 2(b)(iii)'s agency (expressly carved out).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Governing law and forum are stated plainly; 'any claims arising out of or relating to' is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'except as provided in Section 5' carve-out has to accommodate 5(a)'s arbitrations alternating between California and New York and 5(d)'s broad exclusion from arbitration, so the two dispute-resolution schemes interlock imperfectly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability in ordinary terms with no ambiguous operative word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision conflicts with it; it functions as a backstop to the whole instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Which, in order to be effective, or by its nature, must survive' is circular and gives no criterion for identifying surviving terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a termination that the agreement never provides for, since 9(a) grants the licence 'in perpetuity' and no clause permits termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The merger is limited to 'the licensing of the Hard Rock Hotel Marks and Hard Rock Casino Marks' and incorporates an undefined 'Purchase and Sale Agreement', so the integrated whole is not identifiable from the four corners.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reading it with 23's amendment-only-in-writing rule and 21's reference to 'the Morton Parties' and 'the Rank Parties' shows the instrument depends on a companion agreement it never defines, leaving the extinguishment of prior settlement rights contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard successors-and-assigns language; 'as the case may be' adds nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Binding effect on 'transferees and assigns' interacts with 9(c)'s first-offer right and Section 10's sublicence right without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain corporate-authority representation with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements 2(a)'s ownership warranty and 20; no counter-provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The valid and binding agreements of all of the Parties' with a stray comma and a plural 'agreements' in a two-party instrument is untidy but not meaning-changing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Parties' is capitalised but never defined, and the plural 'agreements' hints at the companion Purchase and Sale Agreement referenced in 17; a minor coherence wrinkle.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is a general representation ending in a catch-all — 'any contract, agreement, indenture, lease, promissory note, license or other commitment' — and it uses party labels found nowhere in the operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'The Morton Parties' and 'the Rank Parties' are undefined in this agreement (Section 1 defines only Licensor and Licensee), which points to lifted drafting from the Purchase and Sale Agreement referenced in Section 17.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear waiver formality requirement; the only oddity is 'written notice signed' rather than a signed writing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works alongside 11(b)'s non-waiver clause and 23's amendment formality; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requiring that the Agreement be 'interpreted' only by a written instrument executed by both parties is an unusual word choice that, read literally, purports to bar unilateral or judicial interpretation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That literal reading conflicts with Section 5's arbitration of quality disputes and Section 14's submission of claims to New York courts, both of which necessarily involve interpretation by a third party.
